rationale: The bid-ask spread of 256 bps creates an immediate structural disadvantage — any entry requires price to move roughly 2.56% just to break even on the spread alone, which is nearly double the ATR. The last candle shows a sharp pullback from the session high of $119.37 with very low volume (495 shares), suggesting the momentum spike may be exhausting, but the wide spread makes shorting equally unattractive. With no news catalyst to explain the 6x relative volume surge and no clean risk/reward setup that clears the spread cost within a reasonable ATR-based move, the mechanical edge is insufficient to justify entry in either direction.
